title: Decide the trust boundary of the CORS-open preview/tune artifact write
body:
## Summary
POST /api/preview/tune writes pipeline_artifacts with Access-Control-Allow-Origin * and no operator guard.

## Description
src/app/api/preview/tune/route.ts:16-20 opens the route to any origin and :50 upserts the artifact, while POST /api/pipeline-artifacts is behind requireOperator. The server re-grades, so a pass cannot be forged, but any web page can overwrite a hydratable catalog's step data. requireOperator would refuse the preview game, which runs on another localhost origin, so the fix is a policy: an allow-list of loopback origins or a token (registry technique loopback-addressed-request-gate).

## Flow
- a page on any site POSTs a valid artifact body to localhost
- the preflight passes because of the wildcard
- the step's data is replaced and re-graded

## Expected impact
The operator's tuned data stops being writable from arbitrary sites. An allow-list that misses the preview port would break tuning.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - cross-site writes to artifact data are refused
Before: 1 of 1 tune route open to every origin (read at route.ts:16-20)
After: not built; depends on the allowed-origin decision
Method: simulation - the route was read and no browser was driven; which origins are legitimate is the operator's call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: Decide the allowed preview origins, then pin foreign-origin 403 and preview-origin 200 in a route test

title: Decide whether the paid Scenario route needs the operator guard
body:
## Summary
POST /api/scenario spends on a paid API with no requireOperator and unbounded width/height.

## Description
src/app/api/scenario/route.ts:24 region calls generateTexture for any origin; the night's guard rule names spawn and UE-touching routes, not paid calls. width and height are only typeof-number checked and pass to the provider (src/lib/scenario.ts:91-92). Whether spend counts as privileged is a policy decision.

## Flow
- a cross-site POST with a prompt
- generateTexture spends credits if SCENARIO_API_KEY is set

## Expected impact
Stops drive-by spend. Header-less callers are unaffected while no token is set.

## Evaluation
Claim: cost - cross-site calls cannot spend
Before: 0 of 1 paid route guarded
After: not built
Method: simulation - no paid call may be made in this run
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: Operator ruling on paid routes, then a mocked-generateTexture guard test

title: Validate the gate webhook destination before the server POSTs to it
body:
## Summary
notify/gate stores any string as webhookUrl and the server fetches it.

## Description
src/app/api/notify/gate/route.ts:27-30 only type-checks and trims; src/lib/notify/gate-notifier.ts:49 POSTs to it. file: or malformed values reach fetch and loopback or link-local hosts are reachable (registry technique outbound-fetch-destination-validation). The save POST is also not operator-guarded.

## Flow
- save webhookUrl http://169.254.169.254/x
- Send test
- the server POSTs to that host

## Expected impact
A bad URL is refused at save with a reason. A deliberately local webhook receiver would need an allowance.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - only http(s) destinations of an allowed class are fetched
Before: 0 destination checks between save and fetch
After: not built; the private-host policy is undecided
Method: simulation - two call sites read; no request was sent
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: Route test: non-http scheme -> 400, https accepted, with fetch mocked; private-host handling needs its policy stated first

title: Operator-guard the cook cancel route alongside execute
body:
## Summary
DELETE /api/packaging/cook-jobs kills a running UAT process with no requireOperator.

## Description
src/app/api/packaging/cook-jobs/route.ts:39 cancels a cook. Its sibling execute was guarded in e5ef6d76, but this file is outside this context's file_paths, so it was left unedited.

## Flow
- a cross-site DELETE ?jobId=<id>
- the executor aborts and UAT is killed

## Expected impact
A drive-by request cannot cancel a cook. Same-origin UI is unaffected.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - parity with execute
Before: execute guarded, cook-jobs DELETE not (1 of 2)
After: 2 of 2 expected
Method: simulation - route read; out of this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: Add a cook-jobs case to packaging-operator-guard.test.ts: foreign Origin -> 403, cancel not called

title: Refuse non-string identity fields on checklist/complete and cli-spend
body:
## Summary
The two callback routes check truthiness only, so non-string ids can reach their stores.

## Description
src/app/api/checklist/complete/route.ts only tests presence of moduleId, itemId and projectPath before markComplete. src/app/api/cli-spend/route.ts forwards moduleId, taskType, taskLabel and sessionKey unchecked into recordSpend. Not probed this round.

## Flow
- POST projectPath:42 to checklist/complete
- observe the stored row or a thrown bind

## Expected impact
Callback rows keep their column types. Only malformed callers are affected.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - typed identity columns
Before: unprobed; 2 routes with truthiness-only checks by reading
After: 400 for each non-string id expected
Method: simulation - read only; the round ended before a probe
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Route test with numeric and object ids on both handlers, asserting 400 and no row

title: Answer a corrupt settings blob on profile save with 409 like history
body:
## Summary
profiles POST lets SettingsBlobCorruptError surface as a generic 500.

## Description
src/app/api/packaging/history/route.ts maps SettingsBlobCorruptError to 409 on set-budget. upsertProfile writes through updateSettingsBlob (src/lib/packaging/build-profiles-db.ts:67), which refuses a corrupt row, but src/app/api/packaging/profiles/route.ts has no such mapping, so withRoute answers 500. Inferred by reading; the throw path was not exercised.

## Flow
- corrupt the build_profiles row
- POST a valid profile
- expected 409, read path gives 500

## Expected impact
The UI can report a corrupt store rather than a server fault. Low risk.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - parity of the corrupt-store status
Before: 1 of 2 settings-blob writers maps to 409 (by reading)
After: 2 of 2 expected
Method: simulation - read only; no corrupt row was seeded
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Seed an unparseable build_profiles row in a temp DB and assert 409
